rationale: A defensible composite of two independently validated gates with a sensible coverage fallback, but the liquidity leg (cash net of current debt) partly duplicates the enterprise-value denominator, which already nets cash against debt, so the incremental information may be smaller than the reasoning claims and the triple-rank product risks the same dilution seen in the gen-5 stack.

A legitimate and high-value robustness/coverage test of the archive's largest-alpha signal, though it is close to a mechanical re-run of an already-validated fallback trick, and the fallback (che − dlc) drops the operating-cash-flow term entirely, so the added ~4% of firm-months are gated on a materially different construct than the base sample.

This reduces to value × low net leverage, which is both a well-worn published result (leverage/distress decomposition of B/M) and largely spanned mechanically by the enterprise-yield variants already in the archive, where net debt already sits in the denominator.

The pairing with the net-debt-stock test is a genuinely diagnostic decomposition of the liquidity result and runs at full coverage, but dlc/at is highly collinear with overall leverage, so a positive result will be hard to attribute specifically to rollover risk rather than to the same low-leverage tilt.

A genuinely new cross-market channel — an outside creditor-implied risk opinion rather than another accounting or balance-sheet property of the firm — though xint/(dltt+dlc) is a noisy average rate contaminated by debt maturity mix, intra-year debt changes and capitalized interest, and the sign could equally reflect a low-risk (hence low expected return) tilt, so the result will need that alternative reading ruled out.

Net share issuance interacted with value is a direct rediscovery of the well-documented issuance/composite-issuance anomaly and its standard value interaction, and the construction is flawed because raw GROWTH(csho) is contaminated by splits and stock dividends, which will register as spurious "issuance".
